summary: Le Havre is a dense, cerebral resource-conversion game where you shepherd raw goods through building chains into fish, food, and finished products while carefully managing feeding costs each round. It rewards long-term engine planning over reactive play, and games can run long with real downtime and analysis paralysis, especially at higher player counts.
praised: Deep, satisfying resource-conversion puzzle with meaningful long-term planning
High strategic depth and replayability from variable building sets
Rewards efficient engine-building and multiple viable paths to victory
criticised: Long playtime, especially with more players, exacerbated by analysis paralysis
Steep learning curve and heavy rulebook/iconography to internalize
Low direct player interaction, feels solitaire-ish at the table
Building costs and offer spaces can feel fiddly to track

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light competition for buildings and offer spaces

scoring.why: Final wealth is the sum of cash plus the value of owned buildings and ships, so the winner is whoever built the most efficient, high-value production and ownership engine
